current_disclosures.section: Report of Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm > NOTE 1 Summary of Significant Accounting Principles > Significant Accounting Principles > Loans Held-for-sale
current_disclosures.summary: The Corporation reports loans intended for sale, such as residential mortgages and loan syndications, as Loans Held-for-Sale (LHFS) at the lower of aggregate cost or fair value, with certain residential mortgage LHFS accounted for under the fair value option. Loan origination costs for these assets are capitalized and recognized as part of gain or loss upon sale, while nonperforming LHFS are reported separately from other nonperforming loans and leases.

comparisons.peer_topic: Nonaccrual Loan Criteria and Interest Treatment
comparisons.peer_summary: Loans are placed on nonaccrual status when collection of principal and interest is probable not to occur, triggering reversal of accrued interest and cash-basis recognition or balance reduction; credit card loans accrue interest until paid or charged off, and are considered past due when contractual payments are missed.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and GS define the criteria for placing loans on nonaccrual status based on the probability of collecting principal and interest. BAC states that LHFS on nonaccrual status are reported as nonperforming based on its policy, while GS explicitly details that loans are placed on nonaccrual status when it is 'probable that the firm will not collect all principal and interest due under the contractual terms,' regardless of delinquency. Both entities link nonaccrual status to nonperforming classification, although BAC specifically highlights the separate reporting of these LHFS, whereas GS provides the broader accounting trigger for interest reversal.

sentences.text: LHFS that are on nonaccrual status and are reported as nonperforming, as defined in the policy herein, are reported separately from nonperforming loans and leases.

Loans accounted for at amortized cost (other than credit card loans) are placed on nonaccrual status when it is probable that the firm will not collect all principal and interest due under the contractual terms, regardless of the delinquency status or if a loan is past due for 90 days or more, unless the loan is both well collateralized and in the process of collection.

comparisons.peer_topic: Definition and placement criteria for nonaccrual loans
comparisons.peer_summary: Nonaccrual loans are those on which interest accrual is suspended; they are placed on nonaccrual status when full payment is not expected or when principal/interest is in default for 90+ days, unless well-secured and in collection, with collateral-dependent loans typically maintained on nonaccrual status.
comparisons.comparison: JPM and BAC both identify nonaccrual status as a key component of nonperforming loan classification. BAC discloses that LHFS on nonaccrual status are 'reported as nonperforming,' while JPM defines nonaccrual loans as those where interest accrual is suspended and states they are 'placed on nonaccrual status and considered nonperforming when full payment of principal and interest is not expected.' Both firms use the expectation of collection failure to determine nonaccrual/nonperforming status, aligning on the fundamental risk indicator despite JPM providing more granular timing criteria (90+ days default).

sentences.text: LHFS that are on nonaccrual status and are reported as nonperforming, as defined in the policy herein, are reported separately from nonperforming loans and leases.

Loans (other than credit card loans and certain consumer loans insured by U.S. government agencies) are placed on nonaccrual status and considered nonperforming when full payment of principal and interest is not expected, regardless of delinquency status, or when principal and interest has been in default for a period of 90 days or more, unless the loan is both well-secured and in the process of collection.

comparisons.peer_summary: The Firm places financial instruments on nonaccrual status if principal or interest is past due for 90 days or more or not expected when due, unless the obligation is well-secured and in the process of collection.
comparisons.comparison: MS and BAC align on the use of nonaccrual status as a primary marker for impaired or nonperforming instruments. BAC reports LHFS on nonaccrual status as nonperforming, while MS places financial instruments on nonaccrual status if principal or interest is 'not expected when contractually due.' This shared reliance on the 'not expected' criteria for collection links the two disclosures, although MS applies this to general financial instruments while BAC specifies the treatment for LHFS within its nonperforming definition.

sentences.text: LHFS that are on nonaccrual status and are reported as nonperforming, as defined in the policy herein, are reported separately from nonperforming loans and leases.

The Firm places financial instruments on nonaccrual status if principal or interest is not expected when contractually due or is past due for a period of 90 days or more unless the obligation is well-secured and is in the process of collection.
